record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Construct new explicit examples, in arbitrary dimension and at singular points, of metrics geodesically compatible with gl-regular Nijenhuis operators.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.6. Construct new explicit examples of metrics geodesically compatible with gl-regular operators (at singular points!) in arbitrary dimension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of arbitrary dimension $n$ and let $L:TM\to TM$ be a smooth field of endomorphisms (a $(1,1)$-tensor). The Nijenhuis torsion of $L$ is the $(1,2)$-tensor
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y) = L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY],\quad X,Y\in\Gamma(TM),$$
and $L$ is called a Nijenhuis operator if $\mathcal{N}_L\equiv 0$. The operator $L$ is said to be gl-regular at a point $p\in M$ if the centraliser of $L(p)$ in $\mathrm{End}(T_pM)$ has minimal possible dimension $n$, equivalently if the minimal and characteristic polynomials of $L(p)$ coincide. A point $p\in M$ is a singular point of $L$ if the algebraic type of $L$ (its Jordan structure) is not locally constant at $p$, e.g. eigenvalues collide.

Two pseudo-Riemannian metrics $g$ and $\bar g$ on $M$ are called geodesically equivalent if they share the same unparametrised geodesics. A metric $g$ is said to be geodesically compatible with a Nijenhuis operator $L$ if $L$ is $g$-self-adjoint and the operator $L$ arises (up to standard normalisation) from a metric $\bar g$ geodesically equivalent to $g$ via $L^i_j = (\det(\bar g g^{-1}))^{1/(n+1)} \bar g_{jk} g^{ki}$, equivalently if the pair $(g,L)$ satisfies the classical geodesic-compatibility PDE
$$\nabla_X L = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(X\otimes d(\mathrm{tr}\,L) + (d(\mathrm{tr}\,L)\otimes X)^{\flat}\bigr),$$
where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $g$ and $\flat$ is the index-lowering by $g$.

Problem. Construct new explicit examples, in arbitrary dimension $n\ge 3$, of pairs $(g,L)$ on a neighbourhood of a singular point $p\in M$ such that:
(i) $L$ is a gl-regular Nijenhuis operator on a neighbourhood of $p$,
(ii) $p$ is a singular point of $L$ (the algebraic type of $L$ degenerates at $p$),
(iii) $g$ is geodesically compatible with $L$ in that neighbourhood.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on Nijenhuis geometry (notably the "Applications of Nijenhuis Geometry V" line of work) gives a description of geodesically compatible metrics for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators at algebraically generic points and regular eigenvalue collisions, but explicit constructions at genuine singular points in arbitrary dimension are still missing, and obstructions are known (e.g. diagonal $L=\mathrm{diag}(x,y)$ admits no compatible metric near the origin). The problem of producing such higher-dimensional singular examples is stated as an open research problem and appears unresolved as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Applications of Nijenhuis Geometry V
status_evidence.snippet: Describes geodesically compatible partners for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators; singular collisions raise obstructions.
status_evidence.claim: Description at generic points and certain regular collisions is available, but general singular points remain delicate.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry III: gl-regular Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the theory of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators including behaviour at singular points.
status_evidence.claim: Framework exists but explicit higher-dimensional singular examples of geodesically compatible metrics are not provided.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis Geometry slides (Bolsinov)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open problems including construction of geodesically compatible metrics at singular points in arbitrary dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as open in recent talks.
